title: Test disaster recovery plans
question: Given a recovery objective and test constraint, choose an appropriate exercise type, define success criteria and safety controls, capture results, and turn findings into verified improvements.
scenario: A team performs a parallel recovery test but excludes the identity provider and key-management service because they are operated by other groups.
focalRelation: Record the scope limitation and do not claim end-to-end recovery evidence.

nodes.label: Recovery objective
nodes.detail: Specific service, RTO/RPO, dependency, security, and business acceptance question.

nodes.label: Parallel test
nodes.detail: Recovery components exercised without replacing production traffic.

nodes.label: Identity provider exclusion
nodes.detail: Material trust dependency omitted because another group owns it.

nodes.label: Key service exclusion
nodes.detail: Material decryption/signing dependency omitted from the exercised path.

nodes.label: Measured service criteria
nodes.detail: Observed timing, integrity, authorization, monitoring, capacity, and workflow results.

nodes.label: Owned improvement
nodes.detail: Finding, owner, due date, additional dependency test, plan update, and verified lesson.

states.title: Case facts fixed
states.caption: A team performs a parallel recovery test but excludes the identity provider and key-management service because they are operated by other groups.

states.title: Controlling condition identified
states.caption: A tabletop can reveal coordination gaps without proving technical recovery.

states.title: Tempting shortcut rejected
states.caption: Reading the plan proves recoverability. A read-through proves shared understanding only; technical, dependency, timing, and business acceptance evidence require more realistic testing.

states.title: Bounded action applied
states.caption: Record the scope limitation and do not claim end-to-end recovery evidence. Include or separately test those dependencies, measure service and security criteria, and make the gap an owned improvement before relying on the result for a high-impact recovery claim.

states.title: Outcome accepted with limits
states.caption: Given a recovery objective and test constraint, choose an appropriate exercise type, define success criteria and safety controls, capture results, and turn findings into verified improvements. The case record retains the scope, owner, exceptions, and evidence used for this conclusion.

prediction.prompt: A parallel recovery test excludes identity and key-management services because other teams operate them. What may the report claim?

options.label: Claim end-to-end recovery because the application and database started at the alternate site.
options.feedback: Application start omits identity and key dependencies that may prevent trusted service. The scope cannot support that claim.

options.label: Discard the whole exercise because any excluded dependency makes every observation useless.
options.feedback: Included timing and component results remain useful when accurately bounded; the exclusions become owned follow-up work.

options.label: Report component results and the exclusions; create owned tests for identity and key dependencies.
options.feedback: Correct. The exercise supplies evidence for its measured scope while leaving end-to-end recovery unproven.

prediction.hint: State exactly what was exercised, observed, excluded, and left for follow-up.

transfer.prompt: A full-interruption test would affect life-safety systems and cannot be authorized.

options.label: Use staged or parallel testing, targeted technical tests, simulations
options.feedback: Correct. Use staged or parallel testing, targeted technical tests, simulations, and dependency evidence while documenting the residual assurance gap.

options.label: Reuse the original conclusion because the overall control family is unchanged
options.feedback: Changed fact: A full-interruption test would affect life-safety systems and cannot be authorized. Why this answer fails: “Reuse the original conclusion because the overall control family is unchanged” does not account for that changed condition. Corrected consequence: Record the scope limitation and do not claim end-to-end recovery evidence. Repair target: Decision recomputed — Use staged or parallel testing, targeted technical tests, simulations, and dependency evidence while documenting the residual assurance gap.

options.label: Bypass the normal owner and apply a permanent broad restriction immediately
options.feedback: Changed fact: A full-interruption test would affect life-safety systems and cannot be authorized. Why this answer fails: “Bypass the normal owner and apply a permanent broad restriction immediately” does not account for that changed condition. Corrected consequence: Record the scope limitation and do not claim end-to-end recovery evidence. Repair target: Changed outcome verified — The decision remains provisional until the changed dependency, enforcement result, and accountable evidence are verified.

transfer.hint: Trace the changed fact to the exact decision boundary, then identify the evidence needed before the outcome can be accepted.

retry.prompt: A walkthrough finds that the emergency carrier number is obsolete before any technical recovery step begins. What should happen next?

options.label: Mark the plan successful because no production system was affected
options.feedback: Safety does not make an obsolete required contact a pass.

options.label: Update the owned contact path, verify an alternate, and retest communication
options.feedback: Correct. A walkthrough can validate or fail procedural dependencies even without interrupting production.

options.label: Run a full-interruption test immediately to prove whether the phone number matters
options.feedback: The known contact defect can be repaired and retested without creating unnecessary production risk.

retry.hint: The walkthrough has produced evidence about a communication dependency.

takeaway: Record the scope limitation and do not claim end-to-end recovery evidence.
assumptions: The scenario is a bounded application of the canonical unit, not a universal threshold, legal conclusion, or vendor prescription.
Directed edges carry only their printed relation; proximity and shared color do not imply ownership, authorization, or chronology.
Acceptance applies only to the stated scope and retained evidence; unknown or excluded conditions remain explicit.

learningJob.plainExplanation: A recovery test report must state tested components and excluded dependencies. Application start cannot support an end-to-end recovery claim when identity, keys, safety constraints, or business acceptance were not tested.
learningJob.visualReasoningGain: Aligned test forms and exclusions would let the learner compare what each exercise can prove; the opening objective/test pair does not.
